why_this_tool: AWS Lambda lets you practise the whole delivery problem on one small artifact: a container image, an execution role, configuration injected from outside and a pipeline that promotes into an account you do not own.
alternatives: Google Cloud Run runs any container image and scales to zero with fewer packaging limits; Azure Functions is the closest equivalent for customers on Azure; Kubernetes with Helm, promoted by Argo CD or Flux, fits customers who own the cluster and want pull-based GitOps; Docker with GitHub Actions covers build and pipeline but not hosting; HashiCorp Vault replaces AWS Secrets Manager when secrets must stay cloud-neutral; Sigstore Cosign adds image signing that any of these can verify.

setup.do: Create or reuse an AWS free tier account and set up credentials for a non-root identity on your laptop; no paid service or GPU is needed for this path.
setup.done_when: A caller identity query from your terminal prints the non-root identity you created.

source.title: AWS General Reference - AWS General Reference

setup.why: Every later step signs requests as this identity, and a customer will always hand you a scoped identity, never root.

setup.do: Install a container runtime and the local Lambda development tooling named in the docs so functions can be built and invoked on the laptop.
setup.done_when: The local tooling prints its version and can pull a Lambda base image.

source.title: Development tools for Lambda - AWS Lambda

setup.why: Local emulation lets you practise most of the path without touching a cloud account, which mirrors working before the customer grants access.

setup.do: Read the serverless getting started overview to map which guides cover functions, images and deployment.
setup.done_when: You can name the guide you would open for packaging, for permissions and for deployment.
setup.why: Knowing where each topic lives in the documentation saves time when a customer environment forces you off the default route.

steps.do: Write a minimal function handler that takes a JSON event and returns a JSON reply, then invoke it locally with a sample event.
steps.done_when: The local invoke prints your handler's JSON reply for the sample event.
steps.why: The handler and its event are the smallest unit everything else wraps, so you need to see one run before packaging it.

steps.do: Run the handler several times in a row locally and log when initialisation code runs versus when only the handler runs.
steps.done_when: Your logs show initialisation once and the handler on every invocation.

source.title: Running code with Lambda - AWS Lambda

steps.why: The execution environment lifecycle decides where you load model clients and configuration, and it explains cold start latency a customer will ask about.

steps.do: Package the function as a container image on a Lambda base image, tag it with an immutable version and run that image locally.
steps.done_when: The locally running image answers a test invocation and you can read its digest.
steps.why: The image is the unit of delivery: the same digest must run on your laptop, in your registry and in the customer's registry without a rebuild.

steps.do: Create an execution role that can read exactly one customer's secret, and configure the function to take its environment name and secret name from outside the image.
steps.done_when: The same image returns different settings for two environment values and is denied when asked for another customer's secret.

steps.why: Per customer configuration and secrets must be injected at deploy time so one image serves every environment and no credential is baked in.

steps.do: Compare Lambda Functions and Lambda MicroVMs for an LLM workload and record which one fits a short tool call and which fits a long agent session.
steps.done_when: You have a saved one page comparison with a chosen option and its reason for each of the two workloads.

steps.why: Choosing the compute shape up front is part of serverless delivery, and writing the comparison down gives you a record to revisit per customer.

steps.do: Write a streaming handler that returns a stubbed LLM answer token by token; deploying it needs the free tier account, so use the local stub of the model call as the laptop substitute.
steps.done_when: A client receives the answer in visible chunks instead of one final payload.

source.title: Response streaming for Lambda functions - AWS Lambda

steps.why: Token streaming is where serverless meets LLM systems, and its payload and network limits decide whether Lambda fits the use case.

steps.do: Write an asynchronous version of the model call so the function hands off slow work instead of waiting on it inside one invocation.
steps.done_when: The first function returns immediately and the result arrives through a separate event.

steps.why: Long model calls held open inside a function waste paid time and hit timeouts, a known anti-pattern you will be asked to fix.

steps.do: Compare Lambda with container services for a customer who mandates their own Kubernetes cluster, and load the same image into a local kind cluster as the laptop substitute for a managed cluster.
steps.done_when: The same image digest runs as a pod locally and you have noted which criteria pushed the choice to the cluster.

source.title: Choosing an AWS serverless service - AWS Decision Guides

steps.why: Packaging for a customer cluster starts with knowing when serverless is the wrong target and proving the image is portable to it.

steps.do: Write an infrastructure as code template that declares the function, its image reference, its role and its per customer parameters.
steps.done_when: Deleting the stack and deploying the template again with one parameter file recreates the identical function.

source.title: Development tools for Lambda - AWS Lambda

steps.why: A template makes the deployment reproducible in an account you cannot click around in and turns customer differences into parameters.

steps.do: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the image, publishes it by digest and deploys the template on every merge.
steps.done_when: A merge produces a green workflow run and the deployed function reports the digest that run published.

source.title: Development tools for Lambda - AWS Lambda

steps.why: The vendor side pipeline must produce an artifact a customer pipeline can promote without rebuilding, so automation ends at a pinned digest.

steps.do: Configure a resource-based policy that lets a second identity, standing in for the customer's pipeline account, invoke and promote the function; use a second role in the same account as the laptop substitute.
steps.done_when: The second identity can invoke the function and is denied again once the policy statement is removed.

steps.done_when: A deployment that breaks your chosen control is blocked or flagged and a compliant one passes.
